hypothesis: W-R15's frozen perceptron failed to distinguish mild jittered positives from reorders even though pooled circular mismatch may contain a separable training margin. Compare a single train-only learned threshold with a capacity-matched 16-weight perceptron under unseen jitter and unseen permutation.
freeze: Freeze fresh split, jitter/offset schedules, learning algorithm, labels and thresholds before original run; only development labels can calibrate the threshold. No evaluation-derived adjustment.
population: Same 16x4 W-R11 synthetic sequence, nine entities/seed. Train candidate global offset+17, jitter +/-1, negative alternates reversal/rotate3; heldout offset+61, jitter +/-2, negative even-odd weave. Positive and negative candidates per source have equal multisets and anchors.
arms: 16 copies pooled circular relative mismatch, fixed 32-epoch perceptron
single threshold from development pooled mismatch: theta=(maximum positive training score + minimum negative training score)/2; classify positive if score<=theta even if train distributions overlap
metrics: Per heldout seed full TP/TN/FP/FN, balanced accuracy, dev max positive/min negative gap, exact trained threshold, and every failure.
classification: THRESHOLD_TRANSFER if train-only threshold>=0.85 heldout accuracy and unordered<=0.55; PARTIAL if threshold beats both comparison arms; NEGATIVE otherwise. Preserve class asymmetry.
validation: Pinned W-R15 source, all priors, no future/heldout oracle use, deterministic replay, first-use archive and one full project regression.
claim_limit: Synthetic supervised jitter discrimination, no natural language generalization or accepted-ref change.
